Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acme is ready to move our first privacy-enclave tenant into your private deployment track. Before we start provisioning we'd like a concise list of gating requirements from Redwood so our network and security teams can sign off.

High level items we need from you:
- Expected VPC CIDR ranges to reserve (we have multiple clusters across regions)
- Required firewall/NACL rules and any recommended port whitelist
- IP allowlist for management endpoints and health probes
- Egress control expectations (S3 endpoints, telemetry destinations)
- KMS/HSM integration pattern and key rotation cadence
- Audit log retention and delivery options (Syslog/CloudWatch)

I've attached our current network diagram and the VPC ranges we can spare. Can your team confirm if these are compatible and what exact artifacts we should deliver to speed validation? Also please call out any cert/hostname requirements so we can pre-provision.

We are aiming for tenant provisioning the week of Aug 23 — is that feasible?

Thanks,

Daniel Chu
Director, IT Operations
Acme Health

Subject: Re: Tenant provisioning & network gating for privacy enclave

Thanks Daniel — appreciate the attachments. Looping in Marissa (deploy ops) and Monica (security/compliance) so we can align on the exact gating checklist. Below is the gate list we typically use for privacy-enclave tenants; I pared it down to only what we require for initial provisioning.

Redwood tenant provisioning gate checklist (initial):
1) Account & Identity
   - Dedicated service account for tenant provisioning (IAM role with least privilege)
   - Service account key rotation policy (we require short-lived keys or OIDC flow)
2) Network & Routing
   - Confirm VPC CIDR (no overlap with Redwood control plane ranges). We recommend a /20 or larger per tenant; if you have multiple clusters list them in the CSV.
   - Required subnets: private API subnet(s) + management subnet (for bastion/ops).
   - Route tables: explicit routes for Redwood peering and NAT.
3) Firewall & ACLs
   - Allowlist (egress): management endpoints: 52.34.12.0/24, 34.210.45.0/24 (health & metrics).
   - Ports: TCP 443 (API), TCP 22 (bastion, gated), UDP 123 (NTP) — we recommend NAT for outbound.
4) Peering & DNS
   - VPC peering with our control plane (we provide peering request).
   - Private DNS zone delegation for redwood-managed hostnames (we'll provide zone id).
5) Security & Keys
   - KMS integration: provide key ARN or agree to bring-your-own-key. Key policy must allow Redwood service principal for encrypt/decrypt.
   - TLS: we accept either customer-managed certificate (ACM) for the API endpoint or Redwood-managed certs. Provide CNs/SANs if using customer certs.
6) Logging & Monitoring
   - Audit logs: forward to your Syslog/CloudWatch with 90-day retention minimum; we also support S3 ingestion.
   - Metrics/health: allow our metrics collector to scrape /metrics on 443 from the management subnet.
7) Ops Access & Bastion
   - Bastion jump host IP(s) or zero-trust identity assertion for ops access (we prefer short-lived sessions).
8) Compliance Artifacts
   - SOC2 scope statement or responsible data flow document (if redacted).

Questions for you (please confirm):
- Do the attached VPC ranges include a /20 we can use for the tenant?
- Are you planning to provide a customer-managed KMS key? If yes, share the ARN and key policy reviewer contact.
- Who will own firewall changes — Acme network team or procurement-managed partner?

If all looks good we can schedule a 1-hour provisioning call Aug 17 to walk the teams through the peering request and IAM artifacts.

Marissa/Monica — can you confirm if the two management IP ranges above (52.34.12.0/24 and 34.210.45.0/24) are acceptable to add to Acme's allowlist for the initial health checks?

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
